final_recommendation: The room converged on a trilateral package: 72% auto RVC with 68-70-72 three-year phase-in, immediate labor inspections with automatic fines (appellate review procedurally only, after collection), 16-year term with review gates replacing hard sunset, trilateral appellate panel covering all disputes including Chapter 19, and indexed dairy access capped at 20K tonnes. USTR committed to legal drafting by Friday with explicit language that labor violations do not retroactively trigger RVC acceleration and that appellate panels cannot reduce fines—only send findings back if procedurally flawed.
key_conflicts: Chapter 19 dispute settlement: Canada demanded neutral arbiters and trilateral panel; USTR initially resisted but ultimately accepted trilateral appellate panel covering all disputes
Appellate scope on labor fines: Congress, labor, and industry demanded procedurally-only review (no fine reduction); USTR committed to lock this language in Friday draft
Auto RVC level: Canada pushed for 72% vs. initial 75% demand; compromise reached at 72% with three-year phase-in
key_concessions: USTR: accepted trilateral appellate panel covering all disputes (Chapter 19 preserved), moved from hard sunset to 16-year review mechanism
Canada: accepted 72% auto RVC (up from initial resistance to 75%), accepted indexed dairy access capped at 20K tonnes, accepted automatic labor fines with appellate review after collection
Mexico: accepted automatic fines day one with no delay, accepted appellate review after collection
Auto industry: accepted 72% RVC with three-year phase-in (68-70-72) parallel to immediate labor inspections
red_lines: Canada: Chapter 19 dispute settlement with neutral arbiters (ultimately preserved via trilateral appellate panel)
Labor union & Congress: labor fines must be automatic day one, appellate review procedurally only (cannot reduce fines)
Auto industry: RVC phase-in must be locked in text with no retroactive cross-triggering from labor violations
USTR: labor enforcement kicks in immediately on signature, no delay
ignored_or_underweighted_risks: Fine structure details (percentage vs. fixed amount) raised by dairy and auto but never definitively resolved in transcript
Unanimous vs. majority vote requirement for any fine reduction (supply chain raised but USTR did not explicitly address)
Implementation timeline and supplier contract lock-in risk acknowledged but not fully mitigated beyond Friday legal draft commitment
downstream_risk_variables: Legal drafting quality and speed (Friday deadline creates tight timeline)
Appellate panel composition and procedural rules (scope defined but operational details deferred)
Supplier reorganization costs and timeline (three-year phase-in mitigates but does not eliminate)
Congressional ratification vote (labor enforcement and Chapter 19 compromise designed to secure votes but outcome uncertain)
Mexican domestic ratification of automatic fines and immediate enforcement
uncertainty_notes: Fine structure (percentage vs. fixed) remains unresolved. Unanimous vs. majority vote for any fine reduction raised by supply chain but not explicitly locked. Legal drafting by Friday is ambitious and any breakdown threatens package. Actual appellate panel operational procedures (composition, timeline, procedural standards) deferred to legal text.

marker_evidence.auto_rules_bottleneck: 72% RVC was core negotiation point driving Canada's initial resistance, three-year phase-in (68-70-72) became the concrete compromise that unlocked the package, and auto industry demanded text lock parallel sequencing with labor enforcement
marker_evidence.labor_enforcement_key: Automatic fines day one, indexed wage floors, independent inspections, and procedurally-only appellate review were explicitly tied to Congressional ratification throughout—labor union stated 'Congress kills this' if fines can be reduced, and USTR committed Friday legal draft to lock enforcement language
marker_evidence.canada_dairy_final_issue: Indexed dairy access capped at 20K tonnes was raised and resolved as part of Canada's package, but it did not block progress—Canada accepted it alongside Chapter 19 and RVC concessions without making it a standalone red line
marker_evidence.dispute_settlement_canada_redline: Canada stated 'if dispute settlement is gone, the whole labor enforcement mechanism becomes just another U.S. veto—and that's not a trade agreement' and made Chapter 19 trilateral appellate panel the explicit condition for signing; USTR ultimately accepted trilateral panel covering all disputes
marker_evidence.sunset_to_review_compromise: Supply chain stated 'if it's automatic termination, I'm not retooling plants'—hard sunset was explicitly identified as investment-freezing, and USTR's shift to 16-year term with review gates was the concrete compromise that unlocked capital commitment
marker_evidence.ratification_risk: Congress stated 'if Canada walks, this deal dies trilateral, and Congress won't ratify a U.S.-Mexico-only pact'; labor union and Congress repeatedly tied labor enforcement details (automatic fines, procedurally-only review) to Hill votes; dairy stated 'vague penalties kill ratification'
marker_evidence.supply_chain_adjustment: Auto industry and supply chain raised compliance costs, five-year restructuring timelines, and supplier contract lock-in concerns, but these were acknowledged and mitigated via three-year phase-in rather than driving a major concession or blocking the deal
marker_evidence.us_mexico_first_pressures_canada: Mexico's early acceptance of labor terms and the U.S.-Mexico bilateral forming first was noted (Mexico stated 'we lock this sequencing now, we're signing trilateral within the week'), but Canada's leverage via Chapter 19 red line meant this pressure was acknowledged rather than decisive in forcing Canada's hand
